contract_answer.question: What is the valid CPMLP baseline for Na-ion split 2021 under the v5 locked workflow?
contract_answer.conclusion: CPMLP produced a finite, protocol-compliant split-2021 baseline from the selected epoch-8 checkpoint. Independent recomputation from 600 saved prefix predictions over 6 validation cells gives MAPE 0.126081, Acc@15 0.633333, MAE 24.1698 cycles, and RMSE 30.2755 cycles. Per-cell MAPE/Acc@15 are: 270040-1-6-59 0.094240/0.82; 270040-3-2-55 0.216369/0.00; 270040-3-4-53 0.089252/0.98; 270040-4-2-47 0.260831/0.00; 270040-4-6-43 0.052251/1.00; 270040-5-5-35 0.043543/1.00.

main_symptom: The baseline is accurate overall but its errors are concentrated in two of six validation cells: 270040-3-2-55 and 270040-4-2-47 have MAPE 0.216369 and 0.260831 with zero Acc@15, producing an aggregate signed bias of -21.40 cycles despite the other four cells having MAPE at or below 0.094240.

contradicting_evidence: Cell 270040-1-6-59 has a similarly high target of 201 cycles but only 0.094240 MAPE, so target magnitude alone does not explain the two failures.
All six validation cells belong to the same recorded NA-ion domain, so the evidence does not isolate a domain shift.
causes.interpretation: The aggregate error is not shared uniformly: four cells have MAPE 0.043543-0.094240, whereas two cells contribute MAPE 0.216369 and 0.260831 and are underpredicted by 43.27 and 51.12 cycles on average. On this six-cell split, unresolved cell-condition variation is the strongest observed limitation.
missing_evidence: Matched per-cell condition metadata and nearest training-cell comparisons.
The split-42 and split-2024 repetitions needed to determine whether the same cell pattern persists.

contradicting_evidence: Prefix-bin MAPE is best at cycles 26-50 (0.101571), so prefix dependence is non-monotonic rather than a uniform failure on short histories.
Cached padding is exactly zero and the diagnostic explicitly says sensitivity does not imply future-cycle leakage.
causes.interpretation: MAPE rises from 0.101571 at prefixes 26-50 to 0.143493 at 76-100, and standardized output changes by up to 0.140324 when padding is perturbed. This makes CPMLP's zero-filled flattening path a plausible contributor to late-prefix instability, but it is not a correctness fault.
missing_evidence: A matched architecture ablation that aggregates only observed cycles.
Per-cell prefix curves across the two remaining paper splits.

contradicting_evidence: Training loss fell to 0.389052 of its first-epoch value and the selected checkpoint reached MAPE 0.126081.
causes.interpretation: Predictions show negative mean relative bias (-0.109107), only 0.384120 correlation with targets, and a prediction-to-target standard-deviation ratio of 0.895771. However, connected finite gradients, healthy activations, and substantial loss reduction argue against a dead or numerically failed block; any output compression is more likely statistical than an optimization fault.
missing_evidence: Train-set cell-balanced prediction bias at the selected checkpoint.
Repeated-seed evidence separating sampling variance from representational underfit.

layers.name: intra_embed
layers.role: Embed each cycle's sampled V/I/Q curve before intra-cycle mixing.
layers.reason: Late gradient-to-parameter ratio is 0.003180, late update ratio is 0.000580, near-zero gradient fraction is 0.002220, and activations are finite and non-collapsed.

layers.name: intra_mlp.0
layers.role: Perform the CPMLP intra-cycle residual mixing block.
layers.reason: The block remains connected with late gradient-to-parameter ratio 0.000295 and update ratio 0.0000817; its activation features remain fully active.

layers.name: inter_flatten
layers.role: Flatten the masked cycle representations for inter-cycle prediction.
layers.reason: This path has strong finite gradients and updates with no dead units. Padding sensitivity is a limitation to test in a future matched architecture, not evidence that this valid baseline block is broken.

layers.name: inter_mlp.0
layers.role: Represent the nine-block inter-cycle MLP stack used by CPMLP.
layers.reason: The first and last inter-cycle blocks have finite late gradient-to-parameter ratios of 0.000350 and 0.000592, updates above the frozen threshold, and non-collapsed activations; no gradient-driven repair is justified.

layers.name: head
layers.role: Map the final CPMLP representation to standardized EOL prediction.
layers.reason: The head remains connected and active with finite gradients, late update ratio 0.000102, and no activation collapse; systematic bias is evidence for later comparison, not a validity failure.

screen_floor.reason: NA-E000 is a full-candidate baseline with no reference experiment, so the matched-reference screening floor is not applicable.

next_action.summary: Retain NA-E000 as the valid split-2021 CPMLP baseline and run the identical approved baseline on paper splits 42 and 2024 before reporting the required three-split mean and standard deviation.
